title: Flashforge Adventurer 5M 3D Printer US$159.05 (~A$232.46) with PayPal AU Stock Shipped @ FLASHFORGE 3D Printer Store AliExpress
body:
Deal: Flashforge Adventurer 5M 3D Printer US$159.05 (~A$232.46) with PayPal AU Stock Shipped @ FLASHFORGE 3D Printer Store AliExpress

[internet-stranger] Great price and printer.
I upgraded to the AD5X for multi colour after a few months.
Waiting for a deal on the Creator 5 Pro now…
[BNR32] New to all this but just grabbed the Bambu Lab X2D Combo from todays JB deal. All I'm looking to do is 3d print kids toys but would like multicolour as simple n easy as possible do I cancel?
[3dprintdeals] Pretty much, especially if you stick with PLA.
This has a 220x220x220 print bed compared to the 256x256x256 and it has open sides/top compared to fully enclosed X2D with filtration.
It would be easier to learn with the Bambu though, makerworld ecosystem and Bambu Handy make things almost click & print.
[No Child Support] Phew, almost had buyers remorse on the bambu. Happy to learn on the mini a1 before moving onto bigger printers
[tsk2] you want a proper multi toolhead 3d printer…you will cry with the amount of purge waste with a single toolhead….the 2nd toolhead on x2d is not great.
snap maker u1 or flash-forge creator 5 (dont need the pro if you're not doing abs or asa…but if you want to keep hands out of the printer the enclosure is a good idea).
[bowtiehoon] Good printer, not that hard to work out for me with noob 3d printer experience, wish I spent more for a multi color one though.
[furyou] Newbie here. Multi colour for what usage?
[bowtiehoon] So you can print something with more than one color, I honestly thought I wouldn’t care as I thought it would use it to print the odd missing Lego or broken plastic part. But there are some fun toys and figures to print that look way better with more then one color
[fx82au] finally caved and bought a 3d printer. for about ~$150 after tcb and team ozb it was a no brainer
[Yer] Anycubic PLA/PETG + coins + tbc = $6 a roll!
[Wilburre] Got a link mate? I can't find any that cheap
[Yer] @Wilburre: You'll have to search Anycubic pla/petg on the ali app coin section, there's 2 anycubic shops, one is affiliated and the other is not. No link cos i don't think it will send you to the correct section. Stock and variety isn't great. Geeetech is also on there for around the same price but ive only done a handful of print with it although they all seem fine.
[sauxliu] now for a bigger room to store all my filament!
[knobbs] How does this compare to the other deal today, Bambu labs A1 mini for $266?
This seems to be a bit bigger at 220mm square rather than 180. I have never owned a 3d printer and just getting into it.
[sssx] guess it depends how big the things you want to print are
[knobbs] So it is pretty much same same, this is just bigger?
[sssx] Bambu Labs has been known as the "Apple" of 3d printers, where things "just work" and are easier for beginners compared to other brands. Not sure if the others have been catching up in the past year or two in that regard though, you'd have to do more recent research.
[saintpat] @sssx: I guess that means Prusa would be Xerox PARC, because Apple copied so much from them.
[stevtom27] Worth going pro for enclosure for filter and dust/fume protection?
[3dprintdeals] no, just print out the enclosure or get the kit from Aliexpress.
[Yer] The kit will still require you to print parts, plenty of remixes on printables if you're not keen the file flashforge provides you.
[RooBun] @Yer: Thanks! Any filament recommendations for a beginner pls?
[Yer] @RooBun: PLA is your go to, it'll probably do everything you need for now. By the time you gather more printing experience you'll lean about all the other 1000 filaments available and their strengths and weaknesses.
Edit - If you're talking about printing the enclosure, its recommended to print in PETG due to better heat resistance.
[yippy] @RooBun: I'd just get PETG, just as easy to print as PLA and better heat resistance.
[Wilburre] Top Cashback still work if you use shopping credit for partial payment? The credit is from team ozb from previous purchases during this sale event.
[Yer] Grabbed one of these last time UK cashback was still doable (rip uk tcb) and its super easy to use for my first printer.
[sedi] Bought it for 200 used 2 weeks ago 🙄
Great little printer though,easy to use.
[furyou] Wondering whether to get into this. Every now and then i think if only i had a 3dp, i could make this small item.
But hear that filament has a lifetime, so it would get destroyed by sitting idle for months. And hear it's not food safe, so can't print food containers or bottle caps etc for fridge.
[Domingo] There are food safe filaments, but many filaments are not.
[Mungulz] I’ve had an AD5M for over a year and I smash it, a couple of prints a week, designed some of my own stuff in tinkercad. It’s pretty much bulletproof and I haven’t had any real issues. A couple of times it stopped doing really big prints, so to avoid that if something has 6 large parts I tend to just do 2 or 3 at a time.
Highly recommend at this price point, pretty fast and good quality prints.
[catmao] Never bought anything expensive on AliExpress,how good is the warranty?
[Mungulz] Depends on the seller but my experience has been good. They tend to side with the buyer on refunds and returns in my experience.
[catmao] Thanks, good to know. Never claimed anything as I don't buy expensive items on ali. Bought the mini one at jb and will buy at Ali once we know if we need buy a big printer
[BilboBargains] has the price gone up slightly as i cant get the pricing listed , i see 174.05 after coupon added
[3dprintdeals] Can't wait until Creator 5 Pro is available on Aliexpress AU store, price will be wild
[Krayzii] I know nothing about 3d printers but am curious enough.. is the ongoing cost/part expensive?
[noz] Don't need multicolour, although was tempted to go a Bambu offering for the larger print bed. But settled on this one, as it is still a good upgrade from my existing printer - Aldi Cocoon Create which is almost 10 years old. Upgrading from 180mm to 220mm print bed, and more importantly do away with manual bed levelling!! Also sounds like it will be much faster. Ordered it last night, net cost a bit under $150, crazy price. Thanks OP.
